subject: Music Production
title: Musique Concrète: The First Samplers
description: A short lesson to help you apply Musique Concrète: The First Samplers.

hook.text: In 1948, French composer Pierre Schaeffer recorded train sounds and turned them into a musical piece.

buildup.text: He spliced magnetic tape by hand, looping and rearranging recorded sounds into new compositions.

discovery.text: This technique, called musique concrète, proved any recorded sound could become a musical instrument.

twist.text: Academic critics dismissed it as noise, but it laid the foundation for all modern sampling.

climax.text: Musique concrète showed the world that music did not require traditional instruments at all.

punchline.text: A Frenchman turned train sounds into the first sample.

quiz.question: What did Pierre Schaeffer use for his musique concrète compositions?
options: Spliced magnetic tape of recorded sounds
